subject.title: macOS launchd Gateway still restarts via gateway-update/update.run; document and honor auto-update kill-switch

question: Should `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` also block explicit Gateway control-plane `update.run` managed handoffs under supervised services, or should it remain limited to configured startup/background auto-update applies?
rationale: The narrow code change is straightforward, but it changes the contract of an existing env variable from background auto-update safety to explicit update-request suppression, which automation should not decide without maintainer intent.

options.title: Extend the kill-switch to Gateway update.run
options.body: Gate supervised managed `update.run` handoffs before restart scheduling when `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, update docs, and require launchd proof for the resulting no-restart behavior.

options.title: Keep the kill-switch background-only
options.body: Document that `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` only blocks configured auto-update applies and direct operators to avoid `update.run` or use broader launchd handoff fixes for explicit update requests.

options.title: Introduce a separate explicit-update policy
options.body: Leave `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` as-is and design a new operator policy for control-plane updates, but treat that as a broader config/product change.

recommendation.title: Extend the kill-switch to Gateway update.run
recommendation.body: Gate supervised managed `update.run` handoffs before restart scheduling when `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, update docs, and require launchd proof for the resulting no-restart behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product-contract decision across the core updater and Gateway update surfaces that Peter introduced and recently touched.
